deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X smooth over S, and V a stratified O_X-module, meaning a module with a hyperstratification, i.e. descent data with respect to the formal neighbourhoods of the diagonal. On the previous page, Grothendieck associates to V its de Rham complex Ω·(V) = Ω·_{X/S} ⊗ V. Its differentials are first-order differential operators. He applies the linearization functor (written here Q° or LQ°), which sends a complex of O_X-modules with differential-operator differentials to a complex of stratified modules (M ↦ P^∞_{X/S} ⊗ M, with the canonical stratification). The point is that the stratified cohomology of a linearized module is ordinary Zariski cohomology of M. So the hyper-H_str of Q°[Ω·(V)] is H_DR(X/S, V).

In characteristic 0, the formal Poincaré lemma (circled marginal note on p.13) says that V → Q°[Ω·(V)] is a resolution. Hence H*_DR(X/S, V) ≃ H*_str(X/S, V). Grothendieck stresses that the right-hand side is defined without any reference to differential forms. That is the conceptual gain: de Rham cohomology becomes an intrinsic invariant of the stratified (later infinitesimal/crystalline) site.

Without restriction on the characteristic, the Poincaré lemma fails for the linearized de Rham complex. One then only has a canonical map V → H^0(Q°[Ω·(V)]) compatible with stratifications, i.e. a morphism of complexes of stratified modules V → Q°[Ω·(V)]. Applying H_str to both sides gives a canonical homomorphism H*_str(X/S, V) → H*_DR(X/S, V).

The next page asks whether this is an isomorphism, or even whether H_str is finite-dimensional, in characteristic p (e.g. X an elliptic curve, V = O_X). A margin note says 'surely false; compute for an ordinary elliptic curve'. He also states the programme: H_str is the cohomology of a 'stratifying site', and a variant (the crystalline site with divided powers) should give p-adic cohomology in characteristic p. This page is the motivating comparison step in the 1966-67 'Crystals' lectures.
errors: No mathematical error. The statement that one only gets a map in characteristic p is correct: with naive (non-PD) stratifications the linearized de Rham complex is not a resolution of V. This is exactly the defect later repaired by divided-power envelopes (crystalline Poincaré lemma).
The claim H_str of a linearized module equals Zariski cohomology of the underlying module is used implicitly and not stated on this page.

ideas.what: Comparison H_DR(X/S,V) ≅ H_str(X/S,V) in characteristic 0 via linearization of the de Rham complex and the formal Poincaré lemma
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of infinitesimal (stratified) cohomology with de Rham cohomology; linearization of differential operators
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and de Rham cohomology of schemes, 1966/68); developed by Berthelot and Ogus (infinitesimal site, 1975)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968)

ideas.what: Stratified cohomology is defined without differential forms, making de Rham cohomology intrinsic
ideas.modern_name: Intrinsic definition of de Rham cohomology via the infinitesimal site
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes; also his 1966 letter to Atiyah / IHES Publ. 29 ('On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties')

ideas.what: In arbitrary characteristic only a canonical map H_str → H_DR, induced by V → linearized de Rham complex
ideas.modern_name: Comparison map from infinitesimal/stratified cohomology to de Rham cohomology in characteristic p
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (discussion of characteristic p defects)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard content of Grothendieck's 1966-67 crystals lectures, published in Dix exposés and fully developed by Berthelot and Ogus. The page is a lecture-note draft of a known comparison, and the characteristic p doubts on the next page are also discussed in that published text.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'H^*_{str}(X/S, V)', not 'H^*_{cris}'. The subscript is 'str' (stratified).
'il n'est plus question de [cohomologie, struck] formes différentielles !' — the word is 'différentielles', not 'effectives'.
Insertion above the line reads most likely '{+compatibles aux stratifications+}', not 'filtrations'.
'i.e. des hom. de complexes de Modules {+stratifiés+}' — 'stratifiés', not 'filtrés'; the line begins 'i.e.'.
'd'où en passant aux H_str des deux membres' — likely 'H_str' (or C_str) and 'des deux membres'.
Final boxed formula: 'H^*_{str}(X, V) → H^*_{DR}(X/S, V)'. The original 'X/S' was struck to 'X' and 'str' was added as a circled subscript with an arrow.
